the box covers hosting, a fault response and review requests. That is a fraction of what we actually run, so it reads as website support rather than the retained digital function in DOM-296. The hero sub-line narrows us the same way, to bookings and enquiries.

notes.observation:
This one puts the work on the reader, and it assumes they've already worked out the answer. Most people landing here know what's frustrating them, not what they need, so we're asking for something they haven't got yet. The sub-line adds to it in my opinion: "a clear requirement, or a description of what is happening" reads like a demand before we'll engage.

It's also the last thing they read, so it should feel like the start of something rather than a submission.

Some headings that might work better:

- Tell us where you're taking the business
- Let's talk about what's next
- Start the conversation

And for the sub-line:

- However much or little you've worked out, we'll help you make sense of it. We reply within one working day and agree the next step with you.
- Whether you know exactly what you want or you're still working it out, tell us what's going on and we'll take it from there. We reply within one working day.

I'd lean towards the first, since it reassures them they don't need a spec to get in touch, and that's the real barrier here.

suggested.change: Headings such as 'Tell us where you're taking the business'; sub-line 'However much or little you've worked out, we'll help you make sense of it. We reply within one working day and agree the next step with you.'

notes.observation:
A website subscription is right to say plainly, but as written the catch comes first and the reassurance last, so it's the one box that could read badly. Turning it round keeps the honesty and loses the sting.

The buy-out is tied to "the standard Essential price, currently £1,450. Read strictly, someone on subscription with a Professional-sized site buys it out for the Essential price. Either that's deliberate and should be said, or the buy-out should track whatever tier was built.

Two options: Subscription can be any tier. Then the buy-out is the price of the tier you got, not Essential, and the monthly is probably not flat either.

Subscription is Essential only, and anything bigger has to be bought. Also fine, and worth saying plainly so nobody expects otherwise.

Separately, a reader will do the maths and it currently looks worse than it is. Twelve months at £165 is £1,980, the payments don't count towards ownership, and the buy-out is another £1,450. That reads as £3,430 for a £1,450 site. It's actually defensible, because £95 of the £165 is Partner Pro care, so only £70 a month is the website, but the page never shows that split. Breaking it out would turn a figure that looks steep into one that looks fair.

notes.observation:
Correcting earlier comment: 

I said earlier there was no section explaining what Partner Pro actually does. There is, and it's one of the best pages on the site. Three named plans with prices, what each includes, response times per tier, the takeover process, the Wix and Squarespace move, and the £165 subscription explained properly. The problems that almost nobody will find it.

The only route in is clicking "Look after my existing website" from the four ways in. That's a door for someone who already knows what they want. Nav goes to Pricing, and Pricing shows Partner Pro as one line at £95 with no sign there's a whole page behind it. Anyone arriving to compare, or arriving for a build, never sees any of this. The thing we say we are, the retained relationship, is the hardest thing on the site to reach.

What I'd pull onto the main pricing page:

The three plan names and prices, even as a strip, so £95 isn't a floating number with nothing attached.

One line on what a plan actually covers: hosting, updates, fixes, small edits, bigger work quoted first. That's already written at the top of the Partner Pro page and it's the clearest summary we have.

"Taking over your existing website is included in every plan." That's a strong line and it's invisible from the main page.

A proper link through, not just the route card. Something like "See what a plan covers, month by month."

suggested.change: Pull the three plan names and prices, the one-line cover, 'Taking over your existing website is included in every plan' and a proper link onto the main pricing page.

Either we offer other combinations and should say what they cost, or the subscription really is Essential and Handled only, and that should be said plainly so nobody assumes otherwise.
